research_question: For a pairwise BPR-trained factorization machine on implicit long_view feedback with known item-popularity skew, is there a well-established lightweight technique — e.g. popularity-aware negative sampling (sampling negatives proportional to item popularity rather than uniformly from a user's other impressions) or an inverse-propensity/logit-adjustment correction added to the BPR loss — that measurably improves ranking metrics (AUC/nDCG) over uniform in-user negative sampling, and is it simple enough to implement with numpy only (no exposure/propensity logs beyond in-log item frequency)?
reflection: Iter 4's item-side historical-rate feature overfit (peaked epoch 3, degraded through epoch 8) despite being a reasonable low-variance prior — likely because it's collinear with the video_id embedding itself and just added another path to memorize train-set video quality rather than truly regularizing. Given two code-level attempts (feature_addition, training_procedure/l2 sweep) both failed to beat the accepted BPR-loss change, and I'm flagged as plateaued, I'll use the research budget rather than guess a third variant of a mechanism that hasn't worked yet.

note.title: Propensity-Weighted (Popularity-Based) BPR for Debiasing Popularity Skew — UBPR
note.citation: Saito 2020, ACM ICTIR ("Unbiased Pairwise Learning from Biased Implicit Feedback")
note.tags: BPR, factorization machine, implicit feedback, popularity bias, inverse propensity scoring, negative sampling, unbiased learning to rank, KuaiRand, AUC, nDCG
note.body: Saito (ICTIR 2020) proposes Unbiased BPR (UBPR): instead of changing how negatives are sampled, each observed pairwise (positive-vs-unobserved) term in the BPR loss is reweighted by the inverse of an estimated exposure propensity for the positive item, where propensity is estimated purely from in-log item popularity raised to a tunable power θ (commonly θ≈0.5, following the standard power-law propensity estimator used in unbiased-recommendation literature, e.g. Schnabel et al. and Yang et al.), so no external exposure/click logs beyond item interaction counts are required. This is lightweight (one extra per-item weight array, O(1) lookup per gradient step) and is straightforward to implement with numpy alongside a standard BPR-FM training loop by simply multiplying the sigmoid-gradient term for each positive by 1/propensity(item). The official reference implementation is public at github.com/usaito/unbiased-pairwise-rec, confirming the method's simplicity and reproducibility. Note: search results also surfaced a caveat from a BPR replicability study (arXiv 2409.14217) that plain popularity-based *oversampling of negatives* (Rendle's original adaptive/context-dependent sampler) can underperform uniform sampling on full (non-sampled) ranking metrics — so for a KuaiRand-Pure-style sparse, popularity-skewed long_view task, propensity-reweighting the loss (UBPR-style) is the better-evidenced lightweight fix versus naively skewing negative sampling toward popular items; both approaches only need item interaction-frequency counts, not true exposure logs.
